title: Squat lobsters (Decapoda: Anomura: Munidopsidae) from a natural whale fall on Torishima Seamount, Izu-Ogasawara Arc, northwestern Pacific, with the description of a new species
content:
Abstract
Whale falls in the deep ocean represent a form of chemosynthetic ecosystem that hosts a suite of specialised fauna. We report three species of munidopsid squat lobsters of the genus Munidopsis Whiteaves, 1874 from a natural whale fall in the northwestern Pacific at a depth of 4,021 m on Torishima Seamount, Izu-Ogasawara Arc. These include M. albatrossae Pequegnat & Pequegnat, 1973 and M. tuftsi Ambler, 1980, which represents a westward range extension from Oregon for the latter species, as well as a species new to science. The new species Munidopsis torishimaensis sp. nov. closely resembles M. hirsuta Jones & Macpherson, 2007 and M. profunda Baba, 2005 but differs from M. hirsuta in having the anterobranchial regions less inflated, the antennal spine being much smaller, and the mesial eye spine not exceeding the antennal peduncle. It also differs from M. profunda in the posterior branchial margin of the carapace bearing two spines, the frontal margin with the antennal spine subequal to the anterolateral spine, sternite 3 being divided into two lobes by a wide median notch, sternite 4 with the anterolateral margins nearly straight, the cheliped palm being unarmed, the carpus with only 2 terminal spines, and that the pereopod 2 overreaching cheliped only by the length of dactylus. Molecular data from the mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (COI) gene support the recognition of M. torishimaensis sp. nov. as a new species. Our findings suggest that some species of Munidopsis apparently specialise on whale falls and can have very wide distribution ranges; much remains to be discovered about their species diversity.
